outputs.L2: A process for manufacturing a pre-insulated pipe includes placing a section of jacket pipe (10) within a guide channel (110) that extends between a forward end (111) and a rearward end (112), and securing the jacket pipe section in the channel. A first end (21) of an insulated inner-piping section (20) is then provided, the inner-piping section including an inner pipe enclosed by at least one layer of compressible insulating material (26). At the forward end of the guide channel, the first end of the insulated inner-piping section is introduced into the jacket pipe section. Overpressure is generated at least inside the jacket pipe section and around the inserted first end, at a level sufficient to compress the insulation layer radially. While this pressure is applied, the first end of the insulated inner-piping section is advanced toward the rearward end of the guide channel. The overpressure is subsequently released, thereby securing the insulated inner-piping section within the jacket pipe section and producing the pre-insulated pipe.
outputs.L3:
A length of jacket pipe is first inserted into a guide channel having front and rear ends and secured in place. A length of inner pipe is then provided, with the inner pipe being surrounded by at least one layer of compressible insulation material. A first end of the insulated inner pipe is introduced into the jacket pipe through the front end of the guide channel.

Overpressure is subsequently applied within the jacket pipe, causing the insulation material to compress radially. While the insulation remains compressed, the insulated inner pipe is advanced through the jacket pipe toward the rear end of the guide channel. Once the inner pipe has reached the desired position, the overpressure is removed. The insulation material then expands against the interior surface of the jacket pipe, securing the insulated inner pipe in place and forming a pre-insulated pipe.
outputs.L4:
A pre-insulated pipe assembly is produced by positioning an inner service pipe, surrounded by a layer of compressible thermal insulation, inside an outer jacket pipe. Before insertion, the insulation is wrapped or otherwise arranged around the inner pipe so that its uncompressed outside diameter is greater than the inside diameter of the jacket pipe. This dimensional relationship ensures that the insulation will ultimately fit tightly between the two pipes.

During assembly, an overpressure is applied to the insulation or to a suitable enclosure surrounding the insulation-wrapped inner pipe. The pressure radially compresses the insulation, temporarily reducing its outside diameter sufficiently to allow the inner pipe and insulation to be inserted into the stationary jacket pipe. Because the jacket pipe remains fixed, the insertion operation can be performed in a controlled manner without requiring the outer pipe to be expanded or moved.

Once the insulation-wrapped inner pipe has reached the desired position within the jacket, the applied pressure is released. The resilient insulation then expands radially toward its original dimensions and presses against the inner surface of the jacket pipe. This expansion fills the annular space, holds the inner pipe in position, and creates a stable, close-fitting insulating layer between the inner pipe and the jacket.

The resulting product is a fixed, pre-insulated pipe assembly in which the service pipe, insulation, and protective outer jacket are securely integrated. The method enables efficient assembly while reducing the risk of damaging, displacing, or unevenly compressing the insulation during insertion. It can also provide consistent insulation density and reliable mechanical retention along the length of the finished pipe.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following invention concept into formal patent-claim language: use air overpressure to radially compress insulation around an inner pipe while drawing or pushing it through an outer jacket pipe to produce a pre-insulated pipe.
counterfactuals.output:
### Exemplary Patent Claims

1. **A method of manufacturing a pre-insulated pipe assembly, the method comprising:**  
   positioning thermal insulation around an inner pipe to form an insulated inner-pipe assembly;  
   applying a gaseous pressure greater than ambient pressure to an exterior surface of the thermal insulation so as to radially compress the thermal insulation; and  
   while the thermal insulation is radially compressed, translating the insulated inner-pipe assembly longitudinally relative to an outer jacket pipe to introduce the insulated inner-pipe assembly into the outer jacket pipe.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein translating the insulated inner-pipe assembly comprises drawing the insulated inner-pipe assembly through the outer jacket pipe.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein translating the insulated inner-pipe assembly comprises pushing the insulated inner-pipe assembly through the outer jacket pipe.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein applying the gaseous pressure comprises supplying compressed air to a pressure chamber surrounding at least a portion of the thermal insulation.

5. The method of claim 4, wherein the pressure chamber includes at least one seal configured to restrict escape of the compressed air around the insulated inner-pipe assembly.

6. The method of claim 1, wherein the thermal insulation has, before radial compression, an outside diameter greater than an inside diameter of the outer jacket pipe.

7. The method of claim 6, wherein the gaseous pressure radially compresses the thermal insulation to an outside diameter smaller than the inside diameter of the outer jacket pipe.

8. The method of claim 1, further comprising reducing the gaseous pressure after at least a portion of the insulated inner-pipe assembly has been introduced into the outer jacket pipe, thereby permitting the thermal insulation to expand radially within the outer jacket pipe.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the thermal insulation expands into contact with an inner surface of the outer jacket pipe.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein the thermal insulation comprises a resilient, fibrous, cellular, or porous thermally insulating material.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein the inner pipe, the thermal insulation, and the outer jacket pipe are arranged substantially concentrically.

12. **An apparatus for manufacturing a pre-insulated pipe assembly, the apparatus comprising:**  
    a pressure chamber configured to receive an inner pipe having thermal insulation disposed therearound;  
    a gas supply fluidly coupled to the pressure chamber and configured to establish within the pressure chamber a gaseous pressure sufficient to radially compress the thermal insulation;  
    an outer-jacket support configured to position an outer jacket pipe in longitudinal alignment with the inner pipe; and  
    a translation mechanism configured to move the inner pipe and the radially compressed thermal insulation longitudinally relative to the outer jacket pipe such that the inner pipe and the thermal insulation are introduced into the outer jacket pipe.

13. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the translation mechanism comprises a pulling mechanism configured to draw the inner pipe and the thermal insulation into or through the outer jacket pipe.

14. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the translation mechanism comprises a pushing mechanism configured to push the inner pipe and the thermal insulation into or through the outer jacket pipe.

15. The apparatus of claim 12, further comprising an inlet seal and an outlet seal associated with the pressure chamber and configured to maintain the gaseous pressure while permitting longitudinal movement of the inner pipe and the thermal insulation.

16. The apparatus of claim 12, wherein the pressure chamber includes a compression region disposed adjacent an entrance end of the outer jacket pipe.

17. The apparatus of claim 12, further comprising a guide configured to maintain substantially coaxial alignment among the inner pipe, the thermal insulation, and the outer jacket pipe.

18. **A pre-insulated pipe assembly manufactured according to the method of claim 1, comprising:**  
    an inner pipe;  
    an outer jacket pipe surrounding the inner pipe; and  
    radially resilient thermal insulation disposed in an annular space between the inner pipe and the outer jacket pipe, the thermal insulation having been pneumatically compressed during insertion into the outer jacket pipe.
